title: Rahuvia
dek: A walled valley capital of cherry blossoms, guarded knowledge, sacred thresholds, and the June 2025 peace accord.

facts.Observed features: Walls · cherry blossoms · inner castle · sacred retreat

sources: Rahuvia_Rahu_Capital_Location_and_History.md — supplied 5 October 2026; quest-RP part 024, public observations, attributed Dasa findings, and location safeguards

body:
Rahuvia is the walled capital and spiritual-political center of the Rahu on Prima. Witch Queen Ephraith rules the state whose diplomats, investigators, guards, priests, specialists, and service workers give the city its institutional life.

Behold. Our home. Rahuvia.Hoshi Daemon, 23 June 2025

Hoshi names the city as the peace delegation reaches its walls. Earlier records often say the Rahu capital or Rahuvian capital. Rahuvia names the city; Rahu remains the identity of the people and polity. A scene in Rahu territory is not automatically a scene inside these walls.

A valley road and the remembrance of the dead

The June 2025 delegation follows a road through a mountain valley. Religious statues along the approach serve as prayer sites and guides for souls entering the afterlife. St. Anky asks to pray for those killed on both sides, and Captain Hildethrax approves honoring the dead as good and noble.

The city’s mighty walls mark a defended political center. Their height, thickness, gates, and possible wards are not recorded. Nor are the valley’s name, exact coordinates, population, or travel time from Pristinia.

Cherry blossoms at sunrise

Inside Rahuvia, the rising sun reveals pink cherry blossoms among the streets. Beauty and fortification coexist with ceremony, orderly hospitality, and cultivated civic space. The blossoms give the capital a distinctive observed character, without establishing a formal religious emblem.

Royal Dasa silently attend the visiting delegation. Hoshi orders that guests’ needs be met, and the service appears carefully anticipated. That refinement also brings the people sustaining it into view.

A state with specialized work

Ephraith’s sovereignty works through delegated responsibilities. Ambassador Sophina handles diplomacy; Hildethrax enforces access and arranges practical operations; Strange Talon serves as Master of Intelligence; Yami no Majo represents specialist magical knowledge and cultural instruction. Hoshi Daemon supplies spiritual leadership, while architects, guards, acolytes, and servants carry other work.

The Rahu maintain guarded archives and ancient historical libraries. Rank and belonging affect access, and knowledge is treated as sacred and valuable. The full constitutional hierarchy and the placement of each institution within the city remain unresolved.

Earlier conference rooms and the September 2024 Trial sanctum belong to Rahu institutional life, but their precise relationship to Rahuvia is not established. The older sanctum is not automatically the Queen’s June 2025 retreat.

Service and the people made invisible

Dasa etiquette aims at service that barely interrupts a room. Fans can signal requests, but the complete signaling language is not recovered. Silent attendance and the expectation of near-invisibility are part of the culture visitors encounter.

Lucido Spettoro describes the Dasa as a lowest, numerous labor and service caste and reports magical control. He further alleges that some Rahu construction uses Dasa life-force alongside material and magic; when questioned, he means literal energy rather than simply forced labor.

These are attributed outsider findings. Their scope remains unresolved. They do not establish that every building uses life-force, or that Ephraith, Yami, or the architect Yoshida personally ordered the alleged practice. The claims nevertheless raise a serious question about the cost of Rahuvian order to those doing its least visible work.

The inner castle and sacred retreat

During the peace mission Hildethrax leads the delegation toward the Queen’s retreat. Chakanbi guides them deeper into the castle, past statues, to a sacred bathing ground and changing space. Visitors leave worldly garments behind and receive silvery dark ceremonial robes. Moonlight seems particularly drawn to the changing building.

Entering the temple in other clothing is treated as sacrilegious. Some visitors refuse and withdraw. The scene does not establish a universal mechanical cleansing rule or a complete floor plan.

Hoshi calls the sanctum the holiest of grounds, a place even he does not casually enter. Ephraith is found in prayer. Sacred practice constrains political behavior in the precinct. During this mission, the Rahu hold its religious protection above wartime hostility, granting the enemy negotiators sanctuary within it.

23 June 2025: the capital becomes a place of negotiation

The delegation enters under escort rather than conquering the city. Ephraith and the visitors dispute sovereignty, blame, oathbreaking, repentance, and atonement. Eugene offers his life for another person’s wrongs, and she chooses practical negotiation over his death. Sincere apologies and proposed concessions begin moving the discussion toward peace before Nuru appears.

Nuru’s manifestation changes the evidence and commands good-faith negotiation. Ephraith is visibly shaken and accepts that his wishes must be honored. The scene establishes a turning point rather than a complete account of later Rahu theology.

The resulting terms include ending conflict, ceasing attacks on the Ahau, granting access to Rahu lands and ancient historical libraries, routing future Pristinian-facing business through Eovar, and offering wealth and material cooperation. The full later implementation remains open.

An agreement made sacred

Ephraith takes a ceremonial stone knife from an altar, cuts her palm, and lets blood fall onto the sacred floor. She invokes her forebears against herself if her people break the terms and asks named negotiators to give their own word.

Ancestry, religion, sovereignty, and political obligation meet in this act. Its exact magical enforcement is unknown, and invoking forebears alone does not establish hereditary succession.

24 June 2025: remembering both sides

When Adelia asks about the war dead, Ephraith confirms a burial plot honoring the fallen on both sides and provides a map. Its position inside or outside the city walls is not securely established.

The immediate war ends with an agreement and shared remembrance. Rahuvia’s founding, complete layout, ordinary residential life, later government, the accord’s durability, and any sustained outside access to its libraries remain unresolved.

Craftsmanship at the Rahu visit

Alyhotep asks Shogun Yoshida how Pristinia could learn from Rahu building methods. Yoshida describes inherited craft knowledge, carefully fitted wood and stone, and magic as a tool for precision rather than a substitute for skilled work. These are Yoshida’s explanations; the exchange does not establish that all his claims about Rahu society are true.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4.

A quiet moment at the embassy

At the Longest Night gathering, Cecil and Strange Talon discuss thought, action and the fleeting reflection of stars in the koi pond. Their conversation ends when a cry and splash interrupt the evening. Cecil goes to offer medical help and Talon flies toward the disturbance. Their shared contemplation gives way to duty.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

The road must be found before it can be followed

The peace delegation’s approach is not an uninterrupted walk down a well-known highway. Beyond the first view of the mountains, a waterfall and cliff interrupt the route. The company camps, keeps watch and searches for the way onward. Their old map provides only a presumed border, whose significance Olokun understands as ritual as well as geographical.

Jiangshi eventually finds the concealed beginning of the stone road. It climbs into the mountains toward a waiting Rahu company in ceremonial dress. Hildethrax offers an escort, warning that they will walk through the night. At the next pass, sunrise turns a still pond red and gold beside a lone ceremonial gate.

That threshold is not yet the capital’s wall. Hoshi meets them there, hears objections and gives his account of the conflict, but says the Queen alone can negotiate. He then leads them through a mountain valley, past religious statues, to Rahuvia itself. The successive approaches distinguish the Rahu border, sacred meeting ground and city.

Guests under an enemy’s protection

At the city, Hoshi instructs the attendants to meet the visitors’ needs. Servants appear silently. Sunrise reveals pink cherry blossoms along the streets while the delegation is directed toward the Queen’s retreat. The cultivated city and the people sustaining its hospitality are visible before the negotiations begin.

Chakanbi guides the guests deeper into the castle and to the sacred bathing and changing places. The visitors must decide whether to accept the ceremonial conditions of entry. This is not proof that every Rahu ritual has the same requirements. It is a specific threshold to this audience.

The narrator explicitly distinguishes that sanctuary from the ongoing war: Rahu religious protection holds there, even for enemy negotiators. Hoshi’s earlier readiness to argue gives way to a place he will not enter casually himself. The city’s political meeting is possible partly because its people agree to treat this precinct as sacred.

Other Rahu encounters are not a map of the capital

Separate room records preserve Alyhotep’s discussion with Yoshida and Cecil’s conversation with Strange Talon. They belong to the wider history of Rahu encounters, but the surviving room text does not itself place either conversation inside Rahuvia.

The distinction matters when reading their details. A builder’s explanation can inform what a visitor thinks of Rahu craft without identifying the room as a capital workshop. A koi pond at an embassy is not thereby the city’s sunrise pond or the Queen’s sacred bathing ground. Their related accounts remain below with that location limit.
